sources: dossier=Net position + Required behaviors ('Entry absorption is structural...same rimsky_nodes row...same dispatched run', corroborated across 2026-05-15 and 2026-05-19 artifact entries); doc=delegation.md:13 'The entry does not get its own node — it IS the calling node. Same node, same executor, same parent run.'; code=flatten() (template_validator_graphs.go:145-181) emits the entry's own TemplateNodeDef into spec.Nodes unchanged (confirmed via TestEntryAbsorption_MarkerEmittedOnCallingNode, byType['validate'] present distinct from byType['outer-caller']), and the instance factory (controlapi/instances.go, unconditional loop over tpl.Spec.Nodes) creates a persisted node row for every flattened def including the entry; test=entry_absorption_test.go confirms the entry keeps a distinct TemplateNodeDef post-canonicalization.
note: The doc's 'same node/same row' claim matches dossier-established intent; the code is what drifted — flatten() leaves the entry's own node definition in the canonicalized list instead of dropping it once absorbed, so persistence creates an orphan rimsky_nodes row for the entry (functionally dead since subscriptions to the entry alias resolve via the calling node, but it violates the 'same row' invariant). No doc edit needed; the fix belongs in flatten()/instance-factory code, queued only.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 24 ('Sub-graph RunScope rows are created eagerly...atomic with the internal cascade firing', 2026-05-22 artifact) establishes delegation owns triggering the entry-success internal cascade, not a transition-reason object; doc=delegation.md:20 (pre-fix) claimed ownership of 'the running-to-running transition reason for a sub-graph-internal cascade firing (see concept:transition-reason)'; code=cascade/state.go:32-57 reason enum has no subgraph value and NextState has no running->running edge; subgraph_dispatch.go:134 applies a raw UpdateStateAndOutcome write, not a reason-validated transition; the real marker is the audit event kind for the internal cascade fire; design corpus=transition-reason.md's closed enum also has no subgraph-firing reason, so the doc named an object that exists on neither side.
note: delegation.md named a design object (a transition-reason) that is absent from both code and the concept catalog's own transition-reason definition. Replaced the phantom ownership claim with the dossier-corroborated one: delegation owns triggering the entry-success internal cascade that begins the sub-graph's internal walk.

sources: dossier=silent on this specific gap (no dossier entry addresses unknown-delegate-target validation timing); design corpus=sub-graph.md Boundaries claims sub-graph owns 'the edge-case rejections at registration' and lists five sibling registration-time rejections for other structural sub-graph defects (missing entry/exit, entry==exit, disconnected internals, recursion, main-as-subgraph) with no runtime-only exception carved out; doc=delegation.md:25 invariant 2 already states unknown/non-sub-graph delegate targets are rejected at validation, consistent with that pattern; code=template_validator_graphs.go:163 silently no-ops on an unresolved delegate target (no else-branch error) and detectDelegateCycles:323 continues past unknown targets, so the check is unimplemented; the failure only surfaces at runtime via subgraph_dispatch.go's terminal-apply error.
note: No dossier transcript addresses this directly, but the entire sub-graph/delegation invariant set is uniformly registration-time-rejecting, and sub-graph.md's Boundaries claims exactly this category of rejection as owned. Design-corpus pattern is design-coherent (not suspect), so this clears the provenance gate as artifact-only-but-coherent: the doc's invariant is correct, the code is the missing surface. Direction fix-code, queued only; no doc edit.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 26/Corrections record ('fan-out is literally just an operation that clones a node...distinct things', 2026-06-23 user, transcript) plus the explicit split-settle framing; design corpus=child-execution.md:13 'delegation passes it 1 partition x N children' and :32 'Sub-graph delegation's carry settle fires exactly once per invocation, on the designated exit's terminal' — the real invariant is settle-fires-once, not child-count-one; doc=delegation.md (pre-fix) Definition said 'exactly one child execution' and Invariant 4 said 'Delegation always dispatches exactly one child...the carry mode's one-child requirement...are invariants of concept:child-execution', fabricating a cross-reference to an invariant child-execution.md does not carry.
note: child-execution.md is the naming/invariant owner for the settle primitives and explicitly documents N children under one shared partition, with the real invariant being single-fire settlement, not a one-child dispatch count. Reworded delegation.md's Definition and Invariant 4 to describe one shared child execution context (1 partition x N children) with the carry settle firing exactly once, removing the fabricated 'one-child requirement' cross-reference.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 21 ('Entry absorption: same row, same executor context, same run; caller's holds: merge into the absorbed entry', 2026-05-15+2026-05-19 artifact) names executor and holds explicitly as merging, with nothing suggesting a broader blanket merge of all entry fields; doc=delegation.md:13 (pre-fix) said only 'the entry's sub-graph-internal declarations merged with what the calling node declared externally' with no enumeration; code=absorbEntryIntoCaller (template_validator_graphs.go:202-251) merges exactly Executor, ClaimProducers, Holds, and Attributes.Schema — TemplateNodeDef's other fields (Locks, ErrorTypes, MaxRetries, RetryBackoff, MaxParkDuration, Tags, CascadeMode) are never touched.
note: The vague 'declarations merged' phrasing invited a reader to assume a blanket merge; code (matching the dossier's narrower, named set) merges only four specific fields. Reworded the doc to enumerate exactly what merges (executor, claim-producer bindings, holds bindings, attribute schema) and note other entry-declared fields do not carry over.

sources: dossier=silent (no dossier entry mentions a cascade-boundary-opacity concept); design corpus=cascade.md (full read) contains no occurrence of opacity/opaque/sub-graph/delegation, and its Boundaries own only the firing-gate predicate, the downstream walk, and the two node-level behaviors; a repo-wide grep for 'opacity'/'opaque' across every concept doc finds no concept anywhere defining sub-graph or cascade-boundary opacity; doc=delegation.md:20 (pre-fix) disclaimed 'cascade-boundary opacity (see concept:cascade)' to a neighbor that does not carry it (sub-graph.md's Adjacent list makes the identical dangling reference).
note: No concept in the catalog defines 'cascade-boundary opacity' — the phrase is invented and the pointer dangles at cascade.md, which explicitly says cascade traverses subscription edges 'within and across RunScopes,' i.e. it does not seal boundaries. Removed the phantom disclaim from delegation.md's Does-NOT-own list; concept:cascade remains listed as Adjacent since cascade mechanics are still genuinely relevant to triggering the internal walk. Note: sub-graph.md carries the identical dangling reference in its own Adjacent list but is out of scope for this cluster's edits.

sources: dossier=Intentional absences ('carry_verbatim as an author-facing aggregation-policy value...it was a runtime routing tag, never a policy', 2026-06-19 transcript, user: 'two settlement-mode names...one of those modes has four user-configurable aggregation policies') uses 'settlement mode' loosely in transcript paraphrase, but the later-superseding design corpus fixes the stable name; design corpus=child-execution.md:26 'Owns...the names of their two settle primitives (carry, aggregate)' and :18 'the settle primitive is selected by which dispatch path created the children, not by an author-configured mode' is the concept catalog's naming owner and explicitly rejects mode framing; doc=delegation.md (pre-fix) repeatedly said 'carry settlement mode' at lines 11/14/16 despite its own text later disclaiming configurability.
note: child-execution.md is the design-corpus naming owner for these two primitives and explicitly fixes 'settle primitive' over 'mode' to avoid the configured-mode misreading. delegation.md used 'settlement mode' throughout despite agreeing in substance that it isn't configured — a terminology dialect split against the concept that owns the name. Replaced 'settlement mode' with 'settle primitive' throughout delegation.md.
